messages:
support-bot: Escalation incoming — ACME Prod reporting p95 regressions (~+120ms) after canary rollout v2026.03.14-rc3. Ticket: #12345. Traces: https://telemetry.example/redwood/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:
Maria: Copy — which routes/tenants are impacted? p95 across the board or a cohort?
Kevin: Quick query I ran (Datadog):
```
avg(last_30m):pct(95,service.response_latency{env:canary,route:/v1/generate}) by {tenant}
```
Shows spikes primarily for tenant_acme and tenants with short responses (<8 tokens).
Ashok: Interesting — I compared canary vs stable bucket. Canary p50 ~ equal, p95/p99 driven by a tail for short requests. My hypothesis: new runtime introduced a background kvcache compaction that can preempt small-response fast-paths. I can see occasional 40–120ms sleeps in the runtime logs around compaction events.
Devon: Can you paste the log snippet?
Ashok: 
```
[2026-03-14T12:34:56Z] INFO runtime: kvcache.compact start tenant=tenant_acme dur_hint=5s
[2026-03-14T12:34:56Z] DEBUG runtime: compaction-scan paused fastpath worker pid=2345
[2026-03-14T12:34:56Z] INFO runtime: kvcache.compact end tenant=tenant_acme took=73ms
```
These pauses line up with tail samples.
Maria: Ok — two parallel actions: (1) reproduce locally / in a staging canary node, (2) short-term mitigation (traffic split) and customer comms. @Devon can you run the repro script? I'll open a rollback plan if repro confirms. :+1:
Devon: On it. Repro command I'm running against the canary instance (use the special header to route to canary):
```
# small-response load (1000 qps for 60s)
vegeta attack -rate=1000 -duration=60s -targets=<(echo "GET https://api-staging.redwood/v1/generate\nX-Test-Tenant: tenant_acme\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\"prompt\":\"hi\", \"max_tokens\":2}") | vegeta report -type='hist[0.05,0.50,0.95,0.99]'
```
Running now.
Kevin: If repro reproduces, short-term mitigation: shift 30% of tenant_acme traffic back to stable using traffic-split API: `infra traffic set-split tenant_acme --stable=0.7 --canary=0.3`. Also add a routing rule to prefer fast-path kernel for small responses.
Maria: I can send CS a note: "We've identified a runtime background compaction that affects short responses. We're doing targeted rollback/split and will update within 30m."
Ashok: Another option if rollback is undesirable: flip the runtime flag to disable compaction on canary nodes while we patch. Patch is a configmap change:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-flags -p '{"data":{"kvcache_compaction_enabled":"false"}}'
# then rollout restart runtime-canary
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime-canary
```
This should remove the 50–150ms compaction pauses.
Devon: If we go with patch, need to watch memory growth. I'll instrument memstats and TTL.
Kevin: Also adding a PromQL alert to detect compaction-induced sleeps: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_compact_pause_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant)) > 0.05` — alerts if compaction pause >50ms at p99.
Maria: Status update: Devon reproducing locally, Ashok preparing configmap patch, Kevin prepping traffic-split CLI. I'll coordinate rollback if repro is confirmed.
sre-bot: Automated note — incident channel created: #inc-canary-p95-tail-7401234567. On-call: @Devon.
Devon: Repro done — I see p95 delta ~+110ms with vegeta against canary, stable shows no tail. Will attempt configmap toggle in staging to confirm causality.
Ashok: Confirmed: toggling kvcache_compaction_enabled=false on a single canary node removes the tail in my local run. Patch looks viable.
Maria: Next steps: (1) apply configmap change to canary pool (2) reduce traffic to 0% if any uncertainty, (3) communicate to ACME with rollback/mitigation note. I'll draft the customer message.
Kevin: I'll keep the traffic-split command ready; if patch causes regression elsewhere, we'll abort and rollback the canary release.
Maria: Thanks all — moving this thread to #inc-canary-p95-tail-7401234567 and will update. :white_check_mark:
